run.question: 订单主题的消费滞后是多少

report.summary: The 订单 topic is the Kafka topic `orders` (3 partitions, all led by broker 1, in-sync, none under-replicated or offline). Two consumer groups commit offsets on it. `order-processor` has a total lag of 1100 messages on `orders` (partition 0: 600, partition 1: 0, partition 2: 500), while `order-audit` has a total lag of 0 on `orders` (all three partitions committed up to the end offset). Both groups were EMPTY with no members at the read time, so the lag was not being drained when observed. This is a point-in-time read at about 2026-11-20T21:32:56Z and no historical lag series exists in the queried Prometheus, so when the 1100-message lag accumulated is unknown. No deployment matching an order consumer exists in the cluster as seen now; no root cause is asserted for the lag.

claims.text: Topic `orders` has 3 partitions (0, 1, 2), each with leader 1, replicas [1] and ISR [1], under_replicated=false and offline=false.

Consumer group `order-processor` has total lag 1100 on topic `orders`: partition 0 committed_offset 400 vs end_offset 1000 (lag 600), partition 1 committed_offset 800 vs end_offset 800 (lag 0), partition 2 committed_offset 100 vs end_offset 600 (lag 500); log_start_offset is 0 on all three partitions and no flags are set.
Consumer group `order-audit` has total lag 0 on topic `orders`: committed_offset equals end_offset on every partition (partition 0: 1000/1000, partition 1: 800/800, partition 2: 600/600).
Only two consumer groups consume topic `orders`: `order-audit` (total_lag 0) and `order-processor` (total_lag 1100); both have state EMPTY, member_count 0 and committed_partitions 3.
At the time of reading, the group list shows exactly two classic consumer groups, `order-audit` and `order-processor`, both in state EMPTY (is_simple true).

The cluster's deployment list (all namespaces, 30 deployments) contains no deployment whose name refers to an order consumer; the `otel-demo` namespace deployments are ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping and valkey-cart.

The 1100-message lag on `order-processor` is not being drained because the group has no members (state EMPTY, member_count 0) and no deployment for an order consumer is visible in the cluster now; this could be an intentionally absent consumer rather than a consumer failure, and the evidence cannot distinguish the two.

Topic `orders` itself shows no broker-side fault in this read: every partition has a leader, a full ISR and is neither under-replicated nor offline, so the lag cannot be attributed from this evidence to lost or unavailable partitions.

gaps: The reported lag is one point-in-time read at about 2026-11-20T21:32:56Z; the Kafka tools expose no time range, so the lag during the rest of the authorized window (2026-11-19T21:32:52Z to 2026-11-20T21:32:52Z) is unknown.
Committed and end offsets are read in two separate requests, so the lag is a derived difference rather than a single snapshot.
A Prometheus name query for `kafka.*|.*consumer.*lag.*` returned nothing (status no_data), so no historical lag series was available to date when the 1100-message lag accumulated.
Why `order-processor` has no members is unknown; the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no history of the consumer's removal or scaling is retrievable.
The pod query filtering names matching "order" returned no matches (status no_data), so nothing can be said from it about pods of an order consumer.
Whether the 1100-message lag corresponds to a user-visible problem (e.g. delayed order audit/processing) was not checked; no order-related service error or latency evidence was examined.
next_steps: Confirm with the owning team whether an `order-processor` consumer is supposed to be running and since when it has been absent.
If historical lag matters, expose Kafka consumer-group lag to Prometheus (e.g. kafka-exporter) so lag can be trended over the incident window.
Monitor whether `order-processor` lag continues to grow while the group remains EMPTY, which would indicate orders are accumulating unconsumed.
